serializedLocalizedConversation.mainText:
Landlord: The problem is I didn’t notice your friend leaving, you know? Did she stay for the night?
You: M-maybe?
Landlord: You see, if that would be the case, I’m afraid you would have to pay…{{wi}} a little more. You know, our contract and stuff, hehe~
So that’s what he wants…
Landlord: Oh come on now, don’t make a face like that. Did you really think I wouldn’t hear you being all chummy with someone? Walls here are pretty thin, Dumbass.
Landlord: I heard you both a long time ago, but I chose to ignore it, because I couldn’t believe that you really got a girl. I just thought that you were doing some weird internet e-sex thing I saw on the news once.
Landlord: Kids these days. Disgusting!
You: Just say what you want. Money? 
Landlord: Yes! A lot of it actually!
Landlord: But that much is not in our contract and contracts are something we all must uphold. Am I right?
You: Yes…{{wi}} Yes you are…
Landlord: Glad to hear that. With this out of the way…{{wi}} Here, I brought a copy for you too, just so it’s quicker.
Landlord: Ahem! ‘According to paragraph 32 section 6…’ {{wi}}What? You can’t keep up?
Landlord: It starts on page 47. {{wi}}Got it now?
You: Uhh, why are the letters so small? 
Landlord: I lowered the font to use less paper. What? You don’t care about the planet?!
I don’t think he’s done it because of his good heart…{{wi}} Cheapskate…
You: A-alright, got it.
Landlord: ‘Tenant…’ that’s you ‘...is obliged to inform the Landlord…’, me ‘...about any new occupant that stays in the rented apartment for longer than 3 nights straight. If this isn’t met, the tenant is bound to pay a 300$ fine for every day of delay.’ 
You: W-wait a minute! Fine? You can’t prove that someone lives with me for that long?!
Landlord: Tsk. Listen kid, we can do this easy way, or the hard way. Further in the document it’s written that for every additional occupant the rent rises by 300$.{{wi}} Plus utilities like water and electricity for a total of 446$. {{wi}}Oh, right, these are now taxed too. 
Landlord: Long story short, what I want from you is to pay me 500$ more going forward. Every. Week.
You: 500$?! That’s a robbery!
